issues.legal_issue: Municipal officers do not commit contempt by recommending revocation of a planning scheme or by failing to direct an operator to stop activity when they lack authority to issue that direction.
material_facts: The officers called a municipal meeting at which the council recommended that the planning scheme be revoked.
The officers did not direct the operator to stop exhibiting films, and they had no power to issue such a direction.
issues.conclusion: The officers did not commit contempt.
issues.legal_principle: The court found no contempt in the officers’ conduct: recommending revocation was not disobedience of the judgment, and they could not be held in contempt for failing to issue a direction they had no power to give. No statute or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The matter is an application alleging that persons disobeyed a court judgment.
predicates.municipal_officers_recommended_revocatio: Municipal officers convened a meeting at which the municipal body recommended revoking the relevant planning scheme.
predicates.officers_lacked_power_to_order_cessation: The municipal officers had no authority to direct the operator to stop the activity at issue.
predicates.municipal_officers_not_guilty_of_contemp: The municipal officers are not found guilty of contempt.

issues.definition: When a contempt application concerns officers who recommended revocation and lacked authority to order cessation, those officers are not found guilty of contempt.

issues.legal_issue: An operator commits contempt by continuing to use premises in a way that a court judgment has ruled impermissible when the operator’s licence depended on the authorization invalidated by that judgment.
material_facts: The court had ruled that the building could not be used as a cinema because the resolution authorizing its conversion contravened the planning scheme.
The operator was a party to that judgment and continued exhibiting films in the building under a licence granted on the basis of the invalidated resolution.
The court accepted that the operator believed in good faith that the licence remained effective despite the judgment.
issues.conclusion: The operator was guilty of contempt, although the court accepted the operator’s apology and discharged the rule against him.
issues.legal_principle: The judgment invalidated the authorization on which the licence to exhibit films depended, with the result that the building could not be used as a cinema. The operator was therefore not justified in continuing the exhibitions. The court separately applied the Explanation to Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, which provides that a bona fide apology is not to be rejected merely because it is qualified or conditional.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and court_judgment_barred_the_use and licence_depended_on_invalidated_authorization and operator_continued_the_use

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The matter is an application alleging that persons disobeyed a court judgment.
predicates.court_judgment_barred_the_use: A court judgment ruled that the premises could not be used for the activity in question.
predicates.licence_depended_on_invalidated_authoriz: The operator’s licence was granted on the basis of an authorization that the court invalidated.
predicates.operator_continued_the_use: The operator continued the activity at the premises after the judgment.
predicates.operator_guilty_of_contempt: The operator is found guilty of contempt.

issues.definition: When a contempt application concerns an operator who continues a use barred by a judgment and whose licence depended on invalidated authorization, the operator is found guilty of contempt.

issues.legal_issue: A bona fide conditional apology may be accepted after a finding of contempt, resulting in discharge of the rule against the contemnor.
material_facts: The operator tendered a conditional apology, asking to be pardoned if the court found that he had committed contempt.
The court accepted that the apology was bona fide.
issues.conclusion: The court accepted the apology and discharged the rule against the operator.
issues.legal_principle: The Explanation to Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, states that an apology must not be rejected merely because it is qualified or conditional if it is made bona fide.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The matter is an application alleging that persons disobeyed a court judgment.
predicates.apology_was_conditional: The person tendered an apology that was expressly conditional on the court finding contempt.
predicates.apology_was_bona_fide: The court found that the apology was made in good faith.
predicates.conditional_apology_accepted_and_rule_di: The court accepts the conditional apology and discharges the rule against the person.

issues.definition: When a person in a contempt proceeding offers a bona fide conditional apology, the court accepts it and discharges the rule against that person.

issues.legal_issue: An official does not commit contempt by declining to act on an uncertified copy of a judgment or by renewing a licence for activity permitted under a court order, absent wilful disobedience.
material_facts: The official received a photocopy of the judgment but was told that a certified copy was required for further action; no certified copy or direct communication from the court was provided.
The established practice was not to act on uncertified copies or photocopies of court orders.
The official renewed the licence only for a period during which the High Court order permitted the operator to exhibit films.
The official believed in good faith that the High Court order permitted the activity during that period.
issues.conclusion: The official did not wilfully disobey the judgment and did not commit contempt.
issues.legal_principle: Contempt for disobedience requires wilful disobedience. In the circumstances, the official could not legally be held in contempt for declining to act on an uncertified copy without direct court communication, and renewal for a period allowed by the High Court order was not wilful disobedience. No statute or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and official_received_only_uncertified_copy and no_direct_court_communication and licence_period_was_permitted and official_believed_permission_applied

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The matter is an application alleging that persons disobeyed a court judgment.
predicates.official_received_only_uncertified_copy: The official received only an uncertified copy of the judgment and no certified copy was supplied.
predicates.no_direct_court_communication: The relevant court did not directly communicate its order to the official.
predicates.licence_period_was_permitted: The official renewed the licence only for a period during which a court order permitted the activity.
predicates.official_believed_permission_applied: The official believed in good faith that the court order permitted the activity during that period.
predicates.official_not_guilty_of_wilful_contempt: The official is not found guilty of wilful contempt.

issues.definition: When an official in a contempt proceeding has only an uncertified copy, receives no direct court communication, and acts within a period believed in good faith to be permitted by a court order, the official is not found guilty of wilful contempt.
